summary: Solid day for Solflare Packs: @CryptoGrit posted a 1999 1st Edition Diglett (CGC 10) pull from a Solflare pack and got 32 replies, plus lots of friendly reply chatter. Crypto.com's new Rips is now getting news coverage, and Collector Crypt's 30-day pack sales ($202.9M per a DefiLlama-cited post) keep it far ahead of the field. On the mainstream side, scalper anger is loud again: McDonald's Pokémon Happy Meal cards, metal-detector pack searching, and sold-out 30th Anniversary product. Someone even built their own pack-opening app because the real packs are sold out.

top_posts.text: Pulled a Digda this time xD That's Diglett in German. 1999 Base Set, 1st Edition, CGC Gem Mint 10. Another pack rip in @solflare with @Collector_Crypt :)
top_posts.why_it_matters: Organic repeat Solflare Packs pull post from a 10.5k-follower account. Fun, nostalgic, no price talk. Good to engage.

top_posts.text: Pokémon 30th Anniversary packs are sold out everywhere :( So I built my own pack opening app. Holo foil, card flips and rip animations, all powered by @expo and Skia.
top_posts.why_it_matters: Sold-out retail pushing people to digital pack openings. Clean hook for mainstream collectors.

top_posts.text: Hey @McDonalds ... employees already pocketing shit and putting in old happy meal toys when they haven't sold out of the pokemon happy meal and cards yet.
top_posts.why_it_matters: High-reach (23k impressions) anger about missing McDonald's Pokémon cards. Shows how hard fair access is at retail.

top_posts.text: Scalpers ruined pokemon cards for kids... Apparently they use metal detectors to go through individual packs at the store to see which one has those rare cards now...
top_posts.why_it_matters: Pack-searching distrust. Shown odds and sealed digital packs are a direct answer.

top_posts.text: @cryptocom launched Rips within the App, allowing users to open digital packs representing physical trading cards. Users can accept a quoted sell-back offer or request physical delivery, subject to the service's terms.
top_posts.why_it_matters: Crypto.com Rips now covered as news. Same model as ours (sell-back or ship), with a big mainstream app and card rails.

top_posts.text: @Collector_Crypt sold $202.9M of card packs over the last 30 days, per @DefiLlama. That's roughly 63% of the physical TCG category it tracks.
top_posts.why_it_matters: Our pack partner still leads the category by a wide margin. Useful context for partner conversations.

top_posts.text: gacha is building its own tool stack: - @mnstr: scan cards into a portfolio - @packspyofficial: daily hit board - @Rip_Index: @Courtyard_io pulls of the day - @Crypt0bells: bot for $10k+ @Collector_Crypt pulls - @0x_trophy: the gacha times newsletter
top_posts.why_it_matters: Map of the tools that amplify pulls. Getting Solflare Packs pulls onto these boards is cheap reach.

top_posts.text: I'm convinced Pokémon cards will onboard more normies to crypto than every L2 combined. Nobody's mom knows what a wallet is. Everybody's mom knows what a Charizard is.
top_posts.why_it_matters: Matches our Coinflow / mainstream thesis in plain words.

top_posts.text: Ripping a pack of Pokémon cards, but make it cinematic. I'm really going to try staying consistent with my pack opening series, The Regal Card Chronicles.
top_posts.why_it_matters: 'Cinematic' pack opening series. Format we could borrow for demo-pack clips.

top_posts.text: @ToppsFinest17 This is true, but the companies offering digital pack ripping are infinitely worse. They've essentially turned opening sports cards into a slot machine...
top_posts.why_it_matters: Hobby backlash against digital rips as gambling. Keep our copy fun-first, odds shown, 18+.

sources_note: X search via the x connector, posts from 2026-11-11 09:00 UTC to 2026-11-12 ~09:10 UTC, 9 searches. Engagement numbers are as returned by the X API at scan time. Sales and revenue figures are what the cited accounts posted, not verified. @solflare's own posts today were Breakpoint privacy teases, not Packs, so they're left out. Referral-code spam (Tilt Rips, Triumph Rips), restock bots and giveaways were skipped. The @zard launchpad mention is a third-party token promo that says 'powered by @solflare'; worth checking with the team. Creators already in collector-base.csv or in earlier daily files were excluded.
